articles.title: Still standing: persistence traits capture belowground plant functions beyond resource exploration and acquisition

We propose that understanding belowground plant strategies requires embracing additional functional gradients. articles.desc: Nature Ecology & Evolution, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41559-026-03205-z An evaluation of global pressure–response models for predicting local biodiversity finds that ecologically structured models have higher interpolation accuracy than study-centric mixed-effects models, while both model types exhibit low performance when extrapolating to other contexts.

articles.title: A risk framework for addressing nature’s harmful contributions to people
articles.desc: Nature Ecology & Evolution, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41559-026-03225-9 Some aspects of nature can be harmful to people and have become contentious issues in biodiversity research and policy. This Perspective proposes a new conceptual framework for assessing and managing nature’s harmful contributions to people, drawing parallels with the concept of climate risk.

articles.title: Virus-induced DCL2b relocalization strengthens antiviral defence in tomato
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02459-6 Dicer-like (DCL) proteins are central to antiviral RNA silencing, but how they respond to infection remains unclear. We found that viral infection in tomato increases DCL2b transcription and shifts the protein towards the cytoplasm, promoting antiviral silencing while limiting nuclear miR6026 production. This spatial regulation of DCL2b might help balance antiviral defence with plant growth.

articles.title: Northern Hemisphere permafrost vegetation is greening but becoming less resilient
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02467-6 Our satellite-based vegetation analysis reveals that vegetation across Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions has become less resilient since around 2008 despite continued greening. Atmospheric drying is strongly associated with this reversal, and wildfires further reduce resilience. However, most ecosystem models fail to reproduce the observed change.
